chapter: Road shows in the Southwest and Midwest
title: Spikes Brothers' Arizona circuit: saloons, sporting houses and a parade band
summary: Piano-and-drums duo in Arizona, playing with Fatty Arbuckle's group, building a small circuit and a seven-piece street parade band playing marches.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: went back through Arizona and that way, and we played for all of the dances and everything for a year or so, and during that time Fatty Arbuckle and his...had started out as comedian and his...uh...he had a man...his associate was called...his name was Webb, and it was Arbuckle and Webb, and I think Arbuckle was born in...uh...in Arizona ...in Pre...I can't think...
Did you start to say Prescott?

No, it was...Douglas, I think. Anyway (you got it on?), we played in the back end of the saloons and things with he and...Fatty Arbuckle and his partners, and we was the musicians, and we played in several sporting houses doing the...uh...Arizona, just piano and drums, which was a great novelty in those days, and we were hired by everybody where we just couldn't fill the engagements because it was a novelty, piano and drums, and my brother was a good piano player. So then we organized our own shows, and we had our own little circuit from--we'd stay at Bisbee, and we'd go all around Bowie and kinda near Mexico and Tucson and Phoenix and up to Bowie and Stafford and all around, and we'd make that maybe once or twice a year, the little circuit, and then we'd come back to Douglas and stay three or four months and we'd go out again with kinda a little different show, and we had a seven-piece street band that we'd parade and one instrument of each...in each department--one trumpet, alto, baritone, bass and drums, and that was our little parade band.
What kind of music were you playing? Do you remember any of the tunes?
Marches. You know. We'd parade on the street

to draw the crowd. See? And in those little towns we'd be a sensation, coming down the street, playing, you know, and a comedian out in front, leading the band and putting on a lot of fancy steps and dressed like, you know, like a comic and everything.
